subject: WVB 1.36 bounded scalar write-region execution
claim: The Windows bounded scalar runner embeds the source-built compiler verifier, admits exact WVB 1.36 write-region construction only after verification, executes one success and four exact validation outcomes, rejects structural and semantic forgeries, preserves conservative lifetime containment, and retains the inherited WVB 1.33/1.35 scratch matrix without exposing a native address.

runs.target: Compiler-verifier-gated source-built bounded WVB scalar runner
WVB 1.36 source, WVIR, compiler containment, exact scalar outcomes, and malformed rejection
Inherited WVB 1.33 construction and WVB 1.35 immutable scratch observation

limitations: The focused write-region oracle covered 13 source cases, seven malformed WVIR mutations, five malformed WVB mutations, five semantic WVB forgeries, 19 compiler-verifier decisions, five scalar executions, and one runtime mutation; it was not the complete changed-file development plan.
The scalar provider is limited to a 64-byte private heap extent and alignment through 8. Those are oracle bounds, not portable Language 1.0 limits.
The provider carries only private scalar-heap descriptors and exposes no native address, pointer, host handle, or public representation.
Static verifier containment makes aliasing and stale-region states unreachable in this profile; those exact dynamic failures were not forced by the five scalar cases.

The published front door, native lowerer, pointer derivation, authenticated Foreign-call path, migrated runtime or OS boundary, browser and WebAssembly hosts, and operating-system consumers do not admit WVB 1.36.
The run is local Windows development evidence and does not claim Linux reproduction, paired-host conformance, qualification, release, or independent reproduction.
